evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Jeline: 'this could take ten to fifteen minutes of your time. Is that okay?' — framing present but no real pause for confirmation; customer says 'Mm-hmm' and Jeline immediately pivots to 'let me start pickup address' without waiting for explicit buy-in
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Jeline goes straight into 'Alright, let me start pickup address' with no discovery of customer concerns or priorities beyond logistics.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (1BR apartment), floors/stories (6th floor to 2nd floor), rooms (1BR), walking distances (elevator to apartment, parking to elevator), special considerations (60-inch TV, partial packing kitchen-only), additional stops (none), and special items (TV wrapping needs) all covered
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes: 'Instead of moving only we can add packing as well' and later offered full vs. partial packing distinction
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes: 'normally for a one bedroom apartment we see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — hourly rate ($102/hour per mover, $204 for 2), material estimate ($100 for packing), minimum (2.5 hours), and final estimate given: '$1,292 to $1,496' for 5.5–6.5 hours. Personalized to customer's 6th-to-2nd-floor move with partial kitchen packing.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — disclosed no hidden fees ('no credit card fees, no terrible fees, no disassemble or reassemble fee'), mentioned 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments ('after that minimum, the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments'), and trip/material costs upfront
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Jeline moves directly to 'And then, we can put you now on our schedule if you wish to no deposit is required' with no 'Does that feel fair?' or pause for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False — no 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Two Promises section completely skipped.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway — 'Do you have any questions before I let you go?' is the empty-out version, not 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False — no 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' asked
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out — Jeline asks 'would you like to be on the schedule today, Jordan?' but then immediately offers an escape: 'Is it okay, I can just get your like the quote sent to me cause I'm still also price matching with other movers.' Jeline accepts this and pivots to 'I'll send this to your email' instead of pushing for the close.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: True — 'no deposit is required, I just need your verbal confirmation' indicates rate hold, though not called 'rate lock' explicitly
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial — date (October 23rd), arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM), and crew size (2 movers) confirmed; email (Jordan Washington@gmail.com) and no-deposit policy confirmed, but addresses were clarified in a tangled back-and-forth and no crew notes about customer concerns were left (because no concerns were ever surfaced)

top_strength: Jeline gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, floors, distances, TV size, packing scope) and delivered a detailed, anchored, and personalized estimate with full fee transparency and minimum/increment terms, laying a solid foundation for accurate pricing.
coaching_note: Section 2 (Their Concerns) was completely skipped — Jeline never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' before diving into probing, and then skipped both Two Promises (On-Time + Damage Coverage) and the genuine final concerns check ('What's still concerning you?'), leaving the customer with no reassurance and no reason to book on the call rather than shop other quotes.
